To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the vestibular system has a role in the processing of rewards; 2) vestibular stimulation reduces the sensitivity to rewards; 3) the vestibular stimulation affects attentional orienting in a way that is not yet fully clear, but that might be related to its effect on reward processing.
vestibular stimulation decreases the sensitivity to rewards and thus might have a role as a therapeutic intervention to treat patients with abnormal sensitivity to reward.

the vestibular system plays a key role in the modulation of reward sensitivity and attentional orienting, and that this effect is particularly strong when the vestibular system receives afferent inputs from the right side.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the vestibular system as a possible modulator of attentional and motivational processes, and with the role of visuo-vestbular mismatch in the regulation of attention and reward sensitivity.
the role of the brain’s balance system (the vestibular system) in motivation and attention.
the role of the Vestibular system in the modulation of reward-based attention and motivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GVS is a safe and promising tool to enrich our understanding about the neural underpinning of motivation and reward processing, and eventually tackle the treatment of patients with aberrated reward sensitivity.
GVS is able to reduce reward sensitivity, which is in line with previous findings in the field.
vestibular stimulation does not affect attentional orienting per se but modulates reward-related processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vestibular system has an important role in the modulation of motivation and attention.
GVS is a promising tool to modulate attention and motivation, and that the vestibular system has an important role in reward-based processing.
GVS is a safe way to modulate reward sensitivity, and that the vestibular system has a role in the allocation of attention in space, most likely by altering the motivational value of stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vestibular stimulation can be a powerful tool in investigating the interplay between attentional mechanisms and reward processes.
the vestibular system might play a role in modulating reward-based attention, as a result of the evolutionary pressure exerted by the visuo-vestiubular mismatch.
vestibular stimulation might affect motivation and attention in healthy individuals.
